leads.feed_title: Chevron to relocate 180 California workers to Texas as headquarters move continues

reported_plan.company_characterization: relocation, not a layoff or termination

leads.primary_lead: Article attributes the count, schedule, and company characterization to a California EDD notice, but the exact employer notice has not been retrieved; EDD search results list an official WARN landing page, while third-party indexers label the notice permanent layoffs.
leads.geography_status: Reported planned worker relocation; completion after the expected September 1 start date is unverified as of October 5, 2026.
leads.next_research: Obtain the original EDD employer notice or direct Chevron confirmation; resolve the WARN classification versus the company's quoted relocation description, then verify how many moves actually occurred. Do not report the 180 as completed relocations or layoffs until resolved.

leads.media_claim: The article calls counts of tax returns reporting AGI of at least $1 million “millionaires”: Florida 77,760; Texas 73,930; New York 69,780; California 128,900; it calls tax year 2022 the data vintage.
unresolved: Florida media count differs from IRS AGI_STUB 10 count by 90 returns.
IRS guide is a legacy .doc file; AGI_STUB=10 threshold meaning was not independently decoded in this session.
AGI tax-return counts describe filing units with high reported income, not people, households, net worth, wealth, liquid assets, or millionaires by balance sheet.
leads.next_research: Extract the IRS 2022 codebook and reconcile Florida 77,760 versus 77,670 with the underlying tax-year / filing-year table definition. Only then consider a story titled and described as high-AGI tax returns, never as a wealth count.
